items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-07-01
items.q: INTERVIEWER: What about Big Al Louis Robertson... Do you know him? Sir Robertson, no, I don't know.

ctx.x: Jockey Adams, son sworn he died. Athletic players, but some of the players, some of the men uptown now, some of the old timers that played like him are still living uptown there now, you know.

What about Big Al Louis Robertson, the piano player, not Big Al Louis the clarinet player? Do you know him? Sir Robertson, no, I don't know. What about Cato? Do you know him? Yeah, I know Cato. He's uptown there. Which one? Cato. Cato. Big Cato or Little Cato? Big Cato. He's still living. It's still uptown there,

towards the Irish Channel. I'll try to locate him for you if you want. They'll try to locate him for you. Yeah, if you want to cross him. Yeah. You know? Cato and then there. Old timers, old timers. They were very popular in that day. Very popular. Oh, they were very popular in that day. Oh, they played with jazz in that day like that. See, if you just get the people with the thought of letting the piano player make his parts, just make his parts, like the other men taking other stuff like that. They had better…
